#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -u

TUNNEL_CONTAINER="cloudflared-webagent-named"
AUTO_RUN_SECONDS="${WEBAGENT_BOOT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-30}"
if ! [[ "$AUTO_RUN_SECONDS" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  AUTO_RUN_SECONDS=30
fi

start_webagent=true
start_tunnel=true
destination="console"
deadline=$((SECONDS + AUTO_RUN_SECONDS))

use_defaults() {
  start_webagent=true
  start_tunnel=true
  destination="console"
}

network_summary() {
  local route interface address gateway connection internet tailscale tunnel

  route="$(ip -4 route show default 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
  interface="$(awk '{for (i=1; i<=NF; i++) if ($i == "dev") {print $(i+1); exit}}' <<<"$route")"
  gateway="$(awk '{for (i=1; i<=NF; i++) if ($i == "via") {print $(i+1); exit}}' <<<"$route")"

  if [[ -n "$interface" ]]; then
    address="$(ip -4 -o addr show dev "$interface" scope global 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 {sub(/\/.*/, "", $4); print $4}')"
    if [[ -d "/sys/class/net/$interface/wireless" ]]; then
      connection="Wi-Fi $interface"
    else
      connection="$interface"
    fi
    connection+=" | ${address:-no IPv4}"
    [[ -n "$gateway" ]] && connection+=" | gateway $gateway"
  else
    connection="Disconnected - no default route"
  fi

  if curl --fail --silent --max-time 2 --output /dev/null https://www.cloudflare.com/ 2>/dev/null; then
    internet="Online"
  else
    internet="Offline or unreachable"
  fi

  if [[ "$(systemctl is-active tailscaled 2>/dev/null)" == "active" ]]; then
    tailscale="Connected | $(tailscale ip -4 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
  else
    tailscale="Stopped"
  fi

  if [[ "$(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Running}}' "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" 2>/dev/null)" == "true" ]]; then
    tunnel="Running | webagent.live"
  else
    tunnel="Stopped (selected to start)"
  fi

  printf 'Live network status\n Network:    %s\n Internet:   %s\n Tailscale:  %s\n Cloudflare: %s' \
    "$connection" "$internet" "$tailscale" "$tunnel"
}

mark_check() {
  if "$1"; then printf '[x]'; else printf '[ ]'; fi
}

mark_radio() {
  if [[ "$destination" == "$1" ]]; then printf '(o)'; else printf '( )'; fi
}

while true; do
  status_text="$(network_summary)"
  remaining=$((deadline - SECONDS))
  if ((remaining <= 0)); then
    use_defaults
    break
  fi

  prompt="${status_text}

Defaults auto-run in ${remaining} seconds: WebAgent + tunnel + command prompt.
Select an item to change it, or choose Run:"

  selection="$(timeout --foreground "${remaining}s" whiptail \
    --title "WebAgent Server" \
    --ok-button "Select" \
    --cancel-button "Terminal" \
    --default-item "run" \
    --notags \
    --menu "$prompt" \
    24 76 7 \
    "webagent" "$(mark_check "$start_webagent") Start WebAgent" \
    "tunnel" "$(mark_check "$start_tunnel") Start permanent Cloudflare tunnel" \
    "console" "$(mark_radio console) Open command prompt after startup" \
    "chromium" "$(mark_radio chromium) Open Chromium after startup" \
    "xfce" "$(mark_radio xfce) Open XFCE desktop after startup" \
    "run" "Run selected options" \
    3>&1 1>&2 2>&3)"
  menu_status=$?

  if [[ $menu_status -eq 124 ]]; then
    use_defaults
    break
  elif [[ $menu_status -ne 0 ]]; then
    exit 10
  fi

  case "$selection" in
    webagent)
      if $start_webagent; then start_webagent=false; else start_webagent=true; fi
      ;;
    tunnel)
      if $start_tunnel; then start_tunnel=false; else start_tunnel=true; fi
      ;;
    console|chromium|xfce)
      destination="$selection"
      ;;
    run)
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

messages=()
errors=()
docker_ready=false
webagent_ready=false
webagent_healthy=false

if $start_webagent || $start_tunnel; then
  for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
    if docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      docker_ready=true
      break
    fi
    sleep 1
  done
  if ! $docker_ready; then
    errors+=("Docker did not become ready within 30 seconds.")
  fi
fi

# The permanent tunnel routes webagent.live to this WebAgent instance, so
# selecting it implicitly starts WebAgent even if that service was cleared.
if $docker_ready && { $start_webagent || $start_tunnel; }; then
  if ! docker container inspect webagent >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    errors+=("The WebAgent container does not exist.")
  elif [[ "$(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Running}}' webagent 2>/dev/null)" == "true" ]]; then
    webagent_ready=true
    messages+=("WebAgent was already running.")
  elif docker start webagent >/dev/null; then
    webagent_ready=true
    if $start_tunnel && ! $start_webagent; then
      messages+=("WebAgent started because the tunnel requires it.")
    else
      messages+=("WebAgent started.")
    fi
  else
    errors+=("WebAgent could not be started. Run: docker logs webagent")
  fi
fi

if $webagent_ready && { $start_webagent || $start_tunnel; }; then
  for _ in $(seq 1 45); do
    if curl --fail --silent --max-time 2 "http://localhost:8080/health" >/dev/null; then
      webagent_healthy=true
      break
    fi
    sleep 1
  done
  if ! $webagent_healthy; then
    errors+=("WebAgent did not become healthy within 45 seconds.")
  fi
fi

if $start_tunnel; then
  if ! $webagent_healthy; then
    errors+=("The permanent tunnel requires a healthy WebAgent container.")
  elif ! docker container inspect "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    errors+=("The permanent Cloudflare tunnel container does not exist.")
  elif [[ "$(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Running}}' "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" 2>/dev/null)" == "true" ]]; then
    messages+=("Permanent Cloudflare tunnel was already running.")
  elif docker start "$TUNNEL_CONTAINER" >/dev/null; then
    messages+=("Permanent Cloudflare tunnel started for webagent.live.")
  else
    errors+=("Permanent Cloudflare tunnel could not be started.")
  fi
fi

if ! $start_webagent && ! $start_tunnel; then
  messages+=("No server services were selected.")
fi

mkdir -p "$HOME/.cache"
{
  printf 'WebAgent boot run: %s\n' "$(date --iso-8601=seconds)"
  printf '%s\n' "${messages[@]}"
  if ((${#errors[@]})); then
    printf '%s\n' "${errors[@]}"
  fi
} >"$HOME/.cache/webagent-boot.log"

if ((${#errors[@]})); then
  whiptail --title "WebAgent startup problem" --msgbox "$(printf '%s\n' "${errors[@]}")" 14 76
  exit 1
fi

case "$destination" in
  chromium) exit 20 ;;
  xfce) exit 21 ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Boot session for the physical console (tty1).
#
# First screen is the persistent boot dashboard: it auto-starts and
# supervises the WebAgent stacks. Leaving it into Chromium or XFCE starts
# that interface; closing it returns here to the dashboard again. Quitting
# to the command prompt drops to a shell (the next fresh login reopens the
# dashboard). If the dashboard cannot run at all the legacy whiptail menu
# takes over as a fallback.
set -u

LOG="$HOME/.cache/webagent-boot.log"
DASH=/usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-dashboard
MENU=/usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-menu
CHROMIUM=/usr/local/bin/webagent-chromium-session

launch_gui() {
  case "$1" in
    20) clear
        echo "Opening Chromium. Close it to return to the boot console."
        startx "$CHROMIUM" -- :0 ;;
    21) clear
        echo "Opening XFCE. Log out to return to the boot console."
        startx /usr/bin/startxfce4 -- :0 ;;
  esac
}

run_dashboard() {
  if [ -x "$DASH" ]; then
    "$DASH"
  else
    return 2
  fi
}

# First screen: dashboard, or the legacy menu if the dashboard cannot run.
rc=0
run_dashboard
rc=$?
if [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  clear
  echo "Boot dashboard unavailable - falling back to the classic menu."
  echo
  "$MENU"
  rc=$?
fi

# GUI sessions return to the dashboard when the user closes them.
while [ "$rc" -eq 20 ] || [ "$rc" -eq 21 ]; do
  launch_gui "$rc"
  rc=0
  run_dashboard
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
    clear
    echo "Boot dashboard unavailable - returning to the command prompt."
    break
  fi
done

clear
if [ -f "$LOG" ]; then
  tail -n 30 "$LOG"
  echo
fi
exec /bin/bash -l

"""Presentation client for the protected event-driven v3 boot host."""
from collections import deque
import json,socket,struct
from services import ServiceSpec,RT,Status,Observed
from dockerio import Executor
SERVICES=[
 ServiceSpec("dev-api","dev","app","webagent-dev-v3","API","dev.webagent.live","WebAgent v3 API"),
 ServiceSpec("dev-loop","dev","app","webagent-dev-v3-loop","Loop","dev.webagent.live","WebAgent v3 agent loop"),
 ServiceSpec("dev-gate","dev","app","webagent-dev-v3-gate","Gate","dev.webagent.live","WebAgent v3 publication gate"),
]
class Controller:
    """Cache host-authoritative state; never gather Docker state or plan recovery here."""
    services=SERVICES
    passive=True
    def __init__(self,dry_run=False):
        self.dry_run=dry_run;self.ex=Executor(dry_run=dry_run);self.tick_s=5;self.events=deque(maxlen=6)
        self.rt={s.id:RT() for s in SERVICES};self.obs={};self.statuses={};self.notes={}
    def push(self,msg):self.events.append(msg)
    def request(self,value):
        with socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX,socket.SOCK_STREAM) as peer:
            peer.settimeout(3);peer.connect("/var/lib/webagent/development/boot-supervisor/ui.sock")
            _,uid,_=struct.unpack("3i",peer.getsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_PEERCRED,12))
            if uid!=0:raise ValueError("Boot host identity changed")
            peer.sendall(json.dumps(value).encode()+b"\n")
            raw=peer.makefile("rb").readline(65537)
        if len(raw)>65536 or not raw.endswith(b"\n"):raise ValueError("Boot response bounds")
        reply=json.loads(raw)
        if reply.get("status")!="success":raise ValueError("Boot host rejected request")
        return reply["output"]
    def run_tick(self):
        value=self.request({"operation":"status"})
        for spec in SERVICES:
            item=value["services"][spec.container];o=item["observation"]
            self.rt[spec.id].desired=item["desired"]
            self.obs[spec.id]=Observed(exists=bool(o.get("exists")),running=bool(o.get("running")),
                docker_health=o.get("health",""),http_ok=o.get("health")=="healthy")
            if value["component_paused"]:sev,text=1,"recovery paused: component unavailable"
            elif not item["desired"]:sev,text=3,"off"
            elif item["uncertain"]:sev,text=2,"uncertain: manual action required"
            elif not o.get("exists"):sev,text=2,"container missing"
            elif o.get("health")=="healthy":sev,text=0,"healthy"
            elif o.get("running"):sev,text=1,o.get("health") or "running"
            else:sev,text=1,"stopped: recovery pending"
            self.statuses[spec.id]=Status(sev,text)
    def manual(self,sid,operation):
        spec=next(s for s in SERVICES if s.id==sid)
        if operation=="toggle":operation="stop" if self.rt[sid].desired else "start"
        if self.dry_run:
            message="dry-run: would "+operation+" "+spec.container
            self.push(message);return message
        self.request({"operation":"manual","name":spec.container,"action":operation})
        self.run_tick();return "host accepted "+operation

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""dryrun.py - one live tick against the real server, READ-ONLY.

Docker state is inspected and health endpoints probed, but the controller
runs in dry-run mode: no container is started, stopped or restarted.
Planned actions are listed as "(dry)".

Usage: ./.venv/bin/python dryrun.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from dockerio import Executor
from controller import Controller
from services import SERVICES, SERVICE_BY_ID

SEV = {0: "ok ", 1: "busy", 2: "BAD ", 3: "off "}


def main() -> int:
    ctl = Controller(Executor(dry_run=True),
                     log_path="/tmp/webagent-boot-dryrun.log")
    ctl.run_tick()
    print("=== live status (dry-run, nothing changed) ===\n")
    for spec in SERVICES:
        st = ctl.statuses.get(spec.id)
        txt = st.text if st else "?"
        sev = st.severity if st else 3
        rt = ctl.rt[spec.id]
        o = ctl.obs.get(spec.id)
        run = "up" if (o and o.running) else "down"
        want = "on" if rt.desired else "off"
        print(f"  {SEV.get(sev, '?')} [{want}/{run}] {spec.title:24s} {txt}")
    notes = ctl.notes
    if notes:
        print("\n=== notes ===")
        for k, v in notes.items():
            print(f"  {SERVICE_BY_ID[k].container}: {v}")
    if ctl.ex.dry_log:
        print("\n=== actions this run WOULD take (dry) ===")
        for cont, act in ctl.ex.dry_log:
            print(f"  {act:8s} {cont}")
    else:
        print("\n=== actions: none needed this tick ===")
    print("\nnet:", ctl.ex.net_summary())
    print("\n=== event feed ===")
    for ev in ctl.events:
        print(" ", ev)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Textual terminal input with real event waits and explicit shutdown wake."""
import os,selectors
from codecs import getincrementaldecoder
from textual.drivers.linux_driver import LinuxDriver
from textual._xterm_parser import XTermParser
from textual._parser import get_time

class IdleLinuxDriver(LinuxDriver):
    """Retain the installed Textual parser; wake only for input or its actual Escape deadline."""
    _input_wake_write=None

    def disable_input(self):
        # Set before waking: the reader must not reenter an infinite select during join.
        try:
            self._stop_input=True
            if self._input_wake_write is not None:os.write(self._input_wake_write,b"x")
        except OSError:pass
        super().disable_input()

    def run_input_thread(self):
        """Use a pipe to interrupt blocking select during suspend/exit; no 10 Hz idle tick."""
        reader,writer=os.pipe2(os.O_CLOEXEC|os.O_NONBLOCK)
        self._input_wake_write=writer;self._stop_input=False
        parser=XTermParser(self._debug);decode=getincrementaldecoder("utf-8")().decode
        try:
            with selectors.SelectSelector() as selector:
                selector.register(self.fileno,selectors.EVENT_READ)
                selector.register(reader,selectors.EVENT_READ)
                while not self.exit_event.is_set() and not self._stop_input:
                    # The parser owns a deadline only for an incomplete sequence (e.g. bare Escape).
                    deadline=parser._timeout_time
                    timeout=None if deadline is None else max(0,deadline-get_time())
                    for key,_ in selector.select(timeout):
                        if key.fd==reader:
                            os.read(reader,4096)
                            continue
                        data=os.read(self.fileno,4096)
                        if not data:return
                        for event in parser.feed(decode(data)):self.process_message(event)
                    for event in parser.tick():self.process_message(event)
        finally:
            self._input_wake_write=None
            os.close(reader);os.close(writer)

Only keyboard input wakes the black screen. Legacy bounce helpers are unused.

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import random

def _fit(raw: str, width: int) -> str:
    """Truncate (or pad) a plain-ASCII line to exactly `width` cells."""
    if width <= 0:
        return ""
    clipped = raw[:width]
    return clipped + " " * (width - len(clipped))


@dataclass
class Bouncer:
    """A point moving in a straight line with specular edge reflection.

    Pure logic (no UI) so the physics is unit-testable: the card travels at
    a fixed angle and velocity, and each edge hit mirrors that axis so it
    leaves bouncing straight into the reflected direction.
    """

    x: float
    y: float
    vx: float
    vy: float
    max_x: int
    max_y: int

    @classmethod
    def make(cls, max_x: int, max_y: int) -> "Bouncer":
        vx = random.uniform(7.0, 13.0) * random.choice((-1, 1))
        vy = random.uniform(7.0, 13.0) * random.choice((-1, 1))
        if max_x <= 0:
            vx = 0.0
        if max_y <= 0:
            vy = 0.0
        return cls(0.0, 0.0, vx, vy, max(0, max_x), max(0, max_y))

    def step(self, dt: float) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
        """Advance for `dt` seconds.

        Returns (hit_left_or_right_edge, hit_top_or_bottom_edge).
        """
        self.x += self.vx * dt
        self.y += self.vy * dt
        hit_x = hit_y = False
        if self.x < 0.0:
            self.x = -self.x
            self.vx = -self.vx
            hit_x = True
        elif self.x > self.max_x:
            self.x = 2.0 * self.max_x - self.x
            self.vx = -self.vx
            hit_x = True
        if self.y < 0.0:
            self.y = -self.y
            self.vy = -self.vy
            hit_y = True
        elif self.y > self.max_y:
            self.y = 2.0 * self.max_y - self.y
            self.vy = -self.vy
            hit_y = True
        self.x = max(0.0, min(float(self.max_x), self.x))
        self.y = max(0.0, min(float(self.max_y), self.y))
        return hit_x, hit_y


class ScreensaverScreen(Screen):
    """Opaque black idle screen with keyboard wake and no display timer."""

    CSS = """
    ScreensaverScreen { background: #000000; }
    """

    def __init__(self, host: object, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self._host = host

    async def on_key(self, event: events.Key) -> None:
        # The wake key is consumed: it must never start/stop a service.
        event.stop()
        event.prevent_default()
        if getattr(self._host, "is_screensaver_up", lambda: False)():
            # pop_screen waits on this screen's pump; await it outside the handler.
            asyncio.create_task(self._host.leave_screensaver())

    def on_mouse_down(self, event: events.MouseDown) -> None:
        event.stop()

    def on_click(self, event: events.Click) -> None:
        event.stop()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the WebAgent boot dashboard. Run with sudo:
#     sudo /home/ar/webagent-boot/install.sh
#
# - backs up every existing boot file to /home/ar/boot-backups/<timestamp>/
# - installs the dashboard launchers (webagent-boot-dashboard,
#   webagent-dashboard, webagent), the session wrapper and the xfce
#   console shortcut into /usr/local/bin
# - leaves the legacy whiptail menu in place as an automatic fallback
set -eu

TS=$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)
BACKUP="/home/ar/boot-backups/$TS"
SRC=/home/ar/webagent-boot/bin

echo "==> Backing up existing boot files to $BACKUP"
mkdir -p "$BACKUP"
for f in \
  /usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-menu \
  /usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-session \
  /usr/local/bin/webagent-chromium-session \
  /usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-dashboard \
  /usr/local/bin/webagent \
  /usr/local/bin/xfce \
  /etc/profile.d/webagent-console-menu.sh
do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    cp -p "$f" "$BACKUP/"
    echo "    backed up $f"
  fi
done
chown -R ar:ar "$BACKUP" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Installing dashboard launchers, session wrapper and xfce"
install -m 0755 -o root -g root "$SRC/webagent-boot-dashboard" /usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-dashboard
install -m 0755 -o root -g root "$SRC/webagent-boot-session"   /usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-session
install -m 0755 -o root -g root "$SRC/webagent-boot-dashboard" /usr/local/bin/webagent-dashboard
install -m 0755 -o root -g root "$SRC/webagent-boot-dashboard" /usr/local/bin/webagent
install -m 0755 -o root -g root "$SRC/xfce" /usr/local/bin/xfce

echo "==> Done. The boot console now opens the dashboard on next login."
echo "    Test it now with:  webagent  or  webagent-dashboard   (needs a real terminal)"
echo "    XFCE desktop from a console:      xfce"
echo "    Rollback:          sudo cp -p $BACKUP/webagent-boot-session /usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-session"

# WebAgent boot dashboard

Replaces the one-shot whiptail boot menu with a persistent console dashboard
that runs on the physical server's tty1 at login.

## What it does

- Opens automatically on the boot console (tty1, no SSH/desktop).
- Immediately starts both stacks in dependency order:

  | # | Service | Container | Serves |
  |---|---------|-----------|--------|
  | 1 | WebAgent (prod) | `webagent` | webagent.live |
  | 2 | Tunnel (prod) | `cloudflared-webagent-named` | |
  | 3 | WebAgent (dev) | `webagent-dev` | dev.webagent.live |
  | 4 | Tunnel (dev) | `cloudflared-webagent-dev-named` | |

- Shows live health per service every ~5s (HTTP readiness probe for apps,
  docker state, latency); host network and Tailscale health appear in
  the two rows below the services (5 = Network, 6 = Tailscale).
- Supervises: a service that should be on but is down/unhealthy is
  restarted automatically (with backoff + a crash-loop guard). Tunnels
  wait for their app to answer the health check, then start by themselves.
- Manual control per row: `s` start, `x` stop, `r` restart, `Space` toggle
  (or click the buttons). Deliberately stopping a service sets it OFF and
  the supervisor will not fight you; stopping an app also takes its tunnel
  down. Manual actions reset the crash guard.
- Rows 5-9 under the services: **5 Network** opens the network manager and
  shows the connected network by **name** (SSID / wired profile, not the IP)
  plus its health in green; **6 Tailscale** has its own line showing online
  state and peer count in green; then **Command prompt**, **XFCE** and
  **Chromium**. The separate "Network Status" lines above the services were
  removed - the row statuses are now the summary.
- Leave buttons (and keys): Command prompt (`q`), Chromium (`b`), XFCE
  (`f`). Chromium/XFCE return to the dashboard when closed. `q` drops
  to a shell; the next fresh console login reopens the dashboard.
- Console shortcuts: `webagent` starts the dashboard
  (`webagent-dashboard` is the same launcher under another name);
  `xfce` starts the XFCE desktop from the console and returns to
  the dashboard when you log out of XFCE.

## Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `services.py` | Stack definitions + pure supervisor planner (no I/O) |
| `dockerio.py` | docker + HTTP probes + network summary |
| `controller.py` | Tick loop: gather, plan, act, log |
| `app.py` | Textual UI (bare-bones) |

| `bin/xfce` | Console shortcut: start the XFCE desktop, return to the dashboard on logout |
| `install.sh` | `sudo` install: backs up + installs root files |
| `tests/` | Headless unit + Pilot tests |

## Network screen (Wi-Fi + Ethernet)

From the boot dashboard press **`n`** (or the **Network** button) to open the
network screen; **`q`**/`Esc` returns.

- **Wi-Fi** (`w`): list of nearby networks (SSID, signal, security, active
  marker). `Enter` connects (masked password prompt for secured networks),
  `r` rescans, `d` disconnects, `f` forgets the selected profile, `o` toggles
  the Wi-Fi radio.
- **Ethernet** (`e`): list of wired devices with state + IP. `Enter` toggles
  connect/disconnect.
- Connecting saves the profile (normal `nmcli` behaviour), so it auto-joins
  after reboots. The netplan-managed profile for the current SSID is
  re-created by netplan after a "forget" - that is expected and shown as-is.

Backing modules: `netio.py` (nmcli wrapper) and `netscreen.py` (the screen).
Tests: `tests/test_netio.py`, `tests/test_pilot_net.py`.

## Black screen on idle

After 60 seconds without keyboard activity, the console goes black. The idle
screen has no widgets, animation, status refresh or display timer. Hidden
dashboard redraws and idle-watch polling are suspended. Service supervision
continues at its existing cadence.

Press any keyboard key to restore the current dashboard. The first key only
wakes the display and cannot start, stop or restart a service. Mouse input does
not wake it. Ctrl+U previews the black screen.

WEBAGENT_BOOT_SAVER_SECONDS changes the timeout; 0 disables blanking.
WEBAGENT_BOOT_SAVER_ANIMATE is no longer used.

The change is presentation-only, outside the v3 broker publication context.
Controller planning, executor authority and service-control behavior are retained.
Tests use fake service executors and verify blank pixels, no hidden redraws,
ongoing supervision, mouse inactivity, keyboard wake and current status on wake.
Live activation still needs a restart that cannot alter legacy containers; the
existing startup preflight proposed legacy starts, so no restart is certified.

## Keyboard-woken idle console
The default dashboard is a status/control client of the protected v3 event-driven boot host. It manages only the development API, agent loop and publication gate; production and retired development containers are untouched. After the configured idle interval it shows a completely black screen. Mouse input does not wake it. Keyboard input refreshes current host status and restores the dashboard. While black it performs no status polling, rendering animation or network presentation probes.

Startup and recovery run independently in webagent-boot-development.service. Docker lifecycle/health events and actual retry deadlines drive it. Native container restart policies still recover exited processes. Host-owned desired state, manual stops, uncertainty and the crash guard survive console/host restarts. A withdrawn/disabled boot engine retains pending state without linked fallback; restoration only resumes eligible desired recovery.

The supported planner lives in the v3 engine catalog: version-1 boot.plan, Rust library webagent-boot-supervisor, confined webagent-boot-service and a trusted host launcher reusing the established pre-exec sandbox. Backend publication, tests and ledger evidence belong to the v3 broker workflow. Existing legacy Controller/FakeExecutor scenarios are retained as characterization; normal console startup uses boot_client.Controller.

The installed Textual Linux driver had a 100 ms input poll even when rendering was
quiet. idle_driver.IdleLinuxDriver uses its existing parser's actual deadline for
incomplete sequences, a shutdown wake pipe, and otherwise a blocking selector.
Presentation timers are paused after the first black frame paints and restored
on wake. This includes network and password screens; masked input is retained.
The originating keyboard event is observed before a modal consumes it, so active
typing prevents premature idle. A real PTY fixture verifies zero idle CPU ticks,
bare-Escape wake and shutdown without a blocked reader.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# WebAgent boot dashboard launcher. Exit 2 tells the session wrapper to
# fall back to the legacy whiptail menu (no UI possible).
set -u
VENV=/home/ar/webagent-boot/.venv/bin/python
APP=/home/ar/webagent-boot/app.py

[ -x "$VENV" ] || exit 2
[ -r "$APP" ] || exit 2
[ -t 0 ] || exit 2
case "${TERM:-}" in
  dumb|"") exit 2 ;;
esac

"$VENV" "$APP" "$@"
rc=$?
case "$rc" in
  0|20|21) exit "$rc" ;;
  *) exit 2 ;;   # unexpected dashboard failure -> fallback menu
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Boot session for the physical console (tty1).
#
# First screen is the persistent boot dashboard: it auto-starts and
# supervises the WebAgent stacks. Leaving it into Chromium or XFCE starts
# that interface; closing it returns here to the dashboard again. Quitting
# to the command prompt drops to a shell (the next fresh login reopens the
# dashboard). If the dashboard cannot run at all the legacy whiptail menu
# takes over as a fallback.
set -u

LOG="$HOME/.cache/webagent-boot.log"
DASH=/usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-dashboard
MENU=/usr/local/bin/webagent-boot-menu
CHROMIUM=/usr/local/bin/webagent-chromium-session

launch_gui() {
  case "$1" in
    20) clear
        echo "Opening Chromium. Close it to return to the boot console."
        startx "$CHROMIUM" -- :0 ;;
    21) clear
        echo "Opening XFCE. Log out to return to the boot console."
        startx /usr/bin/startxfce4 -- :0 ;;
  esac
}

run_dashboard() {
  if [ -x "$DASH" ]; then
    "$DASH"
  else
    return 2
  fi
}

# First screen: dashboard, or the legacy menu if the dashboard cannot run.
rc=0
run_dashboard
rc=$?
if [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  clear
  echo "Boot dashboard unavailable - falling back to the classic menu."
  echo
  "$MENU"
  rc=$?
fi

# GUI sessions return to the dashboard when the user closes them.
while [ "$rc" -eq 20 ] || [ "$rc" -eq 21 ]; do
  launch_gui "$rc"
  rc=0
  run_dashboard
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
    clear
    echo "Boot dashboard unavailable - returning to the command prompt."
    break
  fi
done

clear
if [ -f "$LOG" ]; then
  tail -n 30 "$LOG"
  echo
fi
exec /bin/bash -l

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch the XFCE desktop session from the boot console, then return to
# the WebAgent dashboard when XFCE is closed (log out of XFCE).
#
# Installed by install.sh to /usr/local/bin/xfce.
set -u

if [ -n "${DISPLAY:-}" ]; then
  echo "An X display is already active (DISPLAY=${DISPLAY})." >&2
  echo "Log out of XFCE and use the console instead." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
  echo "Run xfce from a real console." >&2
  exit 1
fi

DASH=/usr/local/bin/webagent-dashboard

clear
echo "Opening XFCE. Log out of XFCE to return to the WebAgent dashboard."
startx /usr/bin/startxfce4 -- :0
rc=$?

# XFCE session ended with a clean logout: bring the dashboard back.
if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -x "$DASH" ] && [ -t 0 ]; then
  clear
  exec "$DASH"
fi
exit "$rc"
